## The `process_data()` documentation

This package provides a general function `process_data()` for the
pre-analysis processing of omics data (e.g., proteomics/metabolomics).
All processing steps are optional and can be tailored to your specific
requirements. This function performs the following processing steps (in
order):

1. Excludes features with extreme missingness based on a specified
   threshold
2. Excludes samples with extreme missingness based on a specified
   threshold
3. Imputes missing values using various methods
4. Transforms the data using specified methods
5. Excludes outlying samples using PCA and LOF
6. Handles matched case-control data to ensure matched samples are
   treated appropriately
7. Corrects for plate/batch effects using specified random and fixed
   effects
8. Centers and scales the data

`process_data()` expects up to three input data frames:

1. **Feature data** (`data`): column 1 = sample IDs; remaining columns =
   numeric feature values.
2. **Feature metadata** (`data_meta_features`): contains a feature ID
   column matching the feature column names in `data`, plus feature-level
   information (e.g., `%` missing, `LOD`). Required for `LOD` imputation
   and plate correction.
3. **Sample metadata** (`data_meta_samples`): contains the sample ID
   column matching `data`, plus sample-level covariates (e.g., `plate`,
   `batch`, `age`, `sex`, `center`, or case-control matching IDs).
   Required for plate correction and matched case-control handling.

It returns a list containing:

1. `df_features`: processed feature data frame
2. `df_meta_samples`: filtered sample metadata
3. `df_meta_features`: filtered feature metadata
4. `plot_samples_outlier`: PCA/LOF outlier plot (when `outlier = TRUE`)
5. `id_exclusions`: a list of excluded IDs:
   - `id_features_exclude`: feature IDs excluded for extreme feature
     missingness
   - `id_samples_exclude`: sample IDs excluded for extreme sample
     missingness
   - `id_samples_outlier`: sample IDs excluded in PCA/LOF analysis
   - `id_samples_casecontrol`: sample IDs excluded because a matched
     case-control partner was excluded

## Preparing the example data

`OmicsProcessing` ships with two synthetic flat example datasets:
`example_proteomics` (an Olink-style case-cohort study with 210 samples
and 40 UniProt proteins on NPX scale) and `example_metabolomics` (an
untargeted LC-MS 1:1 matched case-control study).

For most of this vignette we use `example_proteomics` (case-cohort
design, so `case_control = FALSE`), formatted into the three tables
required by `process_data()`:

```{r setup}
library(OmicsProcessing)

data("example_proteomics")

meta_cols <- c("sample_id", "subcohort", "case_status", "batch", "plate", "center", "sex", "age")
protein_cols <- setdiff(names(example_proteomics), meta_cols)

data_features <- example_proteomics[, c("sample_id", protein_cols)]
data_meta_samples <- example_proteomics[, meta_cols]
data_meta_features <- data.frame(
  UNIPROT = protein_cols,
  missing_pct = colMeans(is.na(example_proteomics[, protein_cols])),
  LOD = apply(example_proteomics[, protein_cols], 2, min, na.rm = TRUE) / 2,
  row.names = NULL
)

dim(data_features)
head(data_meta_samples[, 1:6])
head(data_meta_features)
```

## How to use `process_data()`

All arguments are independent and examples are given below. Each
underlying function (e.g., `impute_data()`) can also be used
independently of `process_data()`.

### Sample and feature exclusions for >10% missingness

```{r missingness}
data_processed <- process_data(
  data = data_features,
  col_samples = "sample_id",
  exclusion_extreme_feature = TRUE,
  missing_pct_feature = 0.1,
  exclusion_extreme_sample = TRUE,
  missing_pct_sample = 0.1
)
```

### Imputation of missing feature data

```{r imputation-mean}
data_processed <- process_data(
  data = data_features,
  col_samples = "sample_id",
  imputation = TRUE,
  imputation_method = "mean"
)
```

If imputing using limit of detection (`"LOD"`), you must provide a
feature metadata table containing the feature ID column and the `LOD`
column:

```{r imputation-lod}
data_processed <- process_data(
  data = data_features,
  data_meta_features = data_meta_features,
  col_features = "UNIPROT",
  col_LOD = "LOD",
  col_samples = "sample_id",
  imputation = TRUE,
  imputation_method = "LOD"
)
```

### Transformation of feature data

Transformation by all `Log10` methods (`"Log10"`, `"Log10Capped"`,
`"Log10ExclExtremes"`) will also perform centering and scaling to a mean
of 0. For Olink NPX data (already on a log2 scale), rank-based inverse
normal transformation (`"InvRank"`) is typically preferred:

```{r transformation}
data_processed <- process_data(
  data = data_features,
  col_samples = "sample_id",
  transformation = TRUE,
  transformation_method = "InvRank"
)
```

### Sample outlier exclusions based on PCA and LOF

Outlier detection runs on complete data, so combine it with missingness
filtering and imputation. Internally this calls
[`outlier_pca_lof()`](../reference/outlier_pca_lof.html) (see the
[Outlier removal](outlier-removal.html) vignette for details on the
PCA + LOF + Tukey methodology, or if you need QC-aware or stratified
outlier detection). `example_proteomics` contains three injected
outlier samples (`PROT_018`, `PROT_095`, `PROT_172`), which are flagged
and removed automatically:

```{r outliers}
data_processed <- process_data(
  data = data_features,
  col_samples = "sample_id",
  exclusion_extreme_feature = TRUE,
  missing_pct_feature = 0.1,
  exclusion_extreme_sample = TRUE,
  missing_pct_sample = 0.1,
  imputation = TRUE,
  imputation_method = "mean",
  outlier = TRUE
)

data_processed$id_exclusions$id_samples_outlier
```

When `outlier = TRUE`, `process_data()` also returns a PCA pair plot
coloured by each sample's Local Outlier Factor (LOF):

```{r outlier-plot, fig.width = 9, fig.height = 8, message = FALSE, warning = FALSE}
data_processed$plot_samples_outlier
```

### Plate correction

You can perform linear mixed-model plate/batch correction via
[`normalization_residualMixedModels()`](../reference/normalization_residualMixedModels.html)
by providing sample and feature metadata tables. Random effects
(`cols_listRandom`) and unwanted fixed effects
(`cols_listFixedToRemove`) are removed, while biological covariates in
`cols_listFixedToKeep` are preserved. If your study also records
injection run order, you can visually inspect before/after feature
profiles with
[`plot_omics_distributions()`](plot-omics-distributions.html):

```{r plate-correction, results = "hide", message = FALSE}
data_processed <- process_data(
  data = data_features,
  data_meta_samples = data_meta_samples,
  col_samples = "sample_id",
  data_meta_features = data_meta_features,
  col_features = "UNIPROT",
  col_LOD = "LOD",
  exclusion_extreme_feature = TRUE,
  missing_pct_feature = 0.5,
  exclusion_extreme_sample = TRUE,
  missing_pct_sample = 0.5,
  imputation = TRUE,
  imputation_method = "LOD",
  transformation = TRUE,
  transformation_method = "InvRank",
  outlier = TRUE,
  plate_correction = TRUE,
  cols_listRandom = c("plate"),
  cols_listFixedToKeep = c("age", "center"),
  cols_listFixedToRemove = c("sex"),
  col_HeteroSked = NULL
)
```

```{r plate-correction-summary}
dim(data_processed$df_features)
data_processed$id_exclusions
```

### Matched case-control handling

In a case-cohort study like `example_proteomics`, excluding a sample
does not affect other participants (`case_control = FALSE`). By
contrast, in a 1:1 matched case-control study, excluding a sample due to
missingness or outlier status requires also excluding its matched
partner.

We can demonstrate this using `example_metabolomics`, which contains 90
matched case-control pairs (alongside 36 pooled QC rows that we remove
before passing study samples into `process_data()`):

```{r case-control}
data("example_metabolomics")

metab_study <- dplyr::filter(example_metabolomics, !is_qc)
metab_features_cols <- resolve_target_cols(metab_study, "@")

metab_features <- metab_study[, c("sample_id", metab_features_cols)]
metab_meta_samples <- metab_study[, c(
  "sample_id", "batch", "plate", "case_status",
  "case_control_match", "center", "sex", "age"
)]
metab_meta_features <- data.frame(
  ID_feature = metab_features_cols,
  missing_pct = colMeans(is.na(metab_study[, metab_features_cols])),
  LOD = apply(metab_study[, metab_features_cols], 2, min, na.rm = TRUE) / 2,
  row.names = NULL
)

metab_processed <- process_data(
  data = metab_features,
  data_meta_features = metab_meta_features,
  data_meta_samples = metab_meta_samples,
  col_samples = "sample_id",
  col_features = "ID_feature",
  exclusion_extreme_feature = TRUE,
  missing_pct_feature = 0.5,
  exclusion_extreme_sample = TRUE,
  missing_pct_sample = 0.5,
  imputation = TRUE,
  imputation_method = "mean",
  transformation = TRUE,
  transformation_method = "InvRank",
  outlier = TRUE,
  case_control = TRUE,
  col_case_control = "case_control_match"
)

metab_processed$id_exclusions
```

### Other options

Centering and scaling can be performed using `centre_scale = TRUE`.
Centering and scaling is performed for log-based transformations at the
point of the transformation, regardless of whether `centre_scale = TRUE`.

The processed data, the IDs for excluded samples and features, and the
outlier plot can be saved to disk by setting `save = TRUE` and providing
output directories via `path_out = "path/to/directory/"` and
`path_outliers = "path/to/directory/exclusions/"`.

## References

1. Application of linear mixed models to remove unwanted variability
   (e.g., batch) and preserve biological variations while accounting for
   potential differences in the residual variances across studies
   (Viallon et al., 2021). The functions implementing this
   (`normalization_residualMixedModels()` and
   `FUNnormalization_residualMixedModels()`) utilise the R packages
   [`{pcpr2}`](https://github.com/JoeRothwell/pcpr2),
   [`{lme4}`](https://github.com/lme4/lme4), and
   [`{nlme}`](https://cran.r-project.org/web/packages/nlme/index.html)
    - Viallon V, His M, Rinaldi S, et al. A New Pipeline for the
      Normalization and Pooling of Metabolomics Data. Metabolites.
      2021;11(9):631. Published 2021 Sep 17.
      [doi:10.3390/metabo11090631](https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC8467830/).
    - `{PCPR2}`: Fages & Ferrari et al. (2014) Investigating sources of
      variability in metabolomic data in the EPIC study: the Principal
      Component Partial R-square (PC-PR2) method. Metabolomics 10(6):
      1074-1083,
      [doi: 10.1007/s11306-014-0647-9](https://link.springer.com/article/10.1007/s11306-014-0647-9)
    - `{lme4}`: Bates, D., Mächler, M., Bolker, B., & Walker, S. (2015).
      Fitting Linear Mixed-Effects Models Using lme4. Journal of
      Statistical Software, 67(1), 1–48.
      [doi.org/10.18637/jss.v067.i01](https://www.jstatsoft.org/article/view/v067i01).
    - `{nlme}`: Pinheiro, J. C. & Bates, D. M. Mixed-Effects Models in S
      and S-PLUS. (Springer, New York, 2000).
      [doi:10.1007/b98882](https://link.springer.com/book/10.1007/b98882)
2. Sample exclusion performed using principal component analyses and a
   local outlier factor (Breunig et al., 2000) using a Tukey rule
   (Tukey, 1977) modified to account for skewness and multiple testing
   (Hubert and Vandervieren, 2008)
    - Markus M. Breunig, Hans-Peter Kriegel, Raymond T. Ng, and Jörg
      Sander. 2000. LOF: identifying density-based local outliers.
      SIGMOD Rec. 29, 2 (June 2000), 93–104.
      [doi.org/10.1145/335191.335388](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/335191.335388)
    - Tukey, J. W. Exploratory Data Analysis. (Addison-Wesley Publishing
      Company, 1977).
    - Hubert, M. and Vandervieren, E., (2008), An adjusted boxplot for
      skewed distributions, Computational Statistics & Data Analysis,
      52, issue 12, p. 5186-5201,
      [EconPapers.repec.org/RePEc:eee:csdana:v:52:y:2008:i:12:p:5186-5201](https://EconPapers.repec.org/RePEc:eee:csdana:v:52:y:2008:i:12:p:5186-5201).
3. The implementation of sample exclusions is from the R package
   [`{bigutilsr}`](https://github.com/privefl/bigutilsr) and is
   described in detail by Florian Privé in
   [this blog post](https://privefl.github.io/blog/detecting-outlier-samples-in-pca/)
